grid_rules: The Alberta Electric System Operator capped new large power users at 1,200 MW for now (Phase 1). All of it is already given to two projects, 970 MW and 230 MW. Bill 8 (Royal Assent Dec 11, 2025) gives priority to data centers that bring their own power.

grid_rules: Under Bill 40 (Royal Assent Dec 11, 2025), the government decides which large power users can connect to the grid. The size thresholds will be set in future regulation, and the Data Center Playbook is still a draft (Aug 2026).
check_status: Checked: Royal Assent Dec 11, 2025; no thresholds set yet (Torys)

grid_rules: Under the Data Centre Framework (Aug 27, 2026), new data centers must supply their own power. Six principles guide approvals, including Canadian ownership and a single provincial intake process.

grid_rules: Under Bill 31, BC opened a competitive process on Jan 30, 2026 to decide which data centers can connect to the grid. Over two years, it allows up to 300 MW for AI data centers and 100 MW for other data centers, and no single project can use more than 145 MW. These limits are cut in half from February 2028.
check_status: Checked: 400 MW total (BC gov), 300/100 split, 145 MW cap, halving 2028 (BLG)

grid_rules: The province held a public consultation (Sept 1 to Oct 2, 2026) on a proposed policy framework. It would set priorities and criteria for new data center projects.

grid_rules: Under Bill 69 (adopted June 2025), a power supplier needs the minister's authorization to supply a data center. A similar rule has applied to projects of 5 MW or more since 2023. Hydro-Québec has proposed a rate of about 13¢/kWh for data centers from Nov 1, 2026. The Régie de l'énergie still has to approve it, with a hearing in fall 2026.
check_status: Checked: Bill 69 June 2025, 5 MW rule from 2023, ~13¢/kWh rate proposed for Nov 1, 2026 (BLG)

grid_rules: Bill 39 (introduced Mar 2026) would put data centers in their own electricity rate class, with a levy of up to 100% of the bill. Its status is unclear: York University says it is not in force, while some news reports say it passed.
